correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the beta-shift prefix/first-return-loop bijection: an allowed n-return loop has floor(n α) ones, prefix length m has ceil(m α), yielding Z(z)=T(z)/(1-L(z)). At z=e^{-tα}, infinitely many fractional hits {nα}<α/2 make L divergent; hence the unique earlier positive root determines pressure. For optimizing invariant measures, the exact loop defect sum forces sublinear short-loop counts and zero frequency of non-Sturmian k-blocks, hence μ_α by unique ergodicity. For bounded partial quotients, rotation max-gap O(1/t) gives c/t lower root and badly approximable orbit separation gives C/t upper root. Convex pressure secants then give the sharp Θ(t^{-2}) derivative/density defect and entropy identity h=D-tD'. Specification/Bowen gives finite-t equilibrium uniqueness. Independently enumerated all binary words lengths 0..11 and matched a separate renewal-polynomial recurrence; source verifies 0..13. These finite checks are not the irrational-slope theorem.
residual_risks: The rotation-gap lemma and count of loop boundaries are the genuinely nontrivial steps; the proof uses standard convergent-denominator bounds but no independent full-text check of Huang et al. Lemma 4.3 was possible.
No precise positive limit of tD(t) is claimed; constants depend on the fixed bounded-type α.

value.rationale: The natural equilibrium response of a Sturmian beta-shift under the simplest local digit observable is not a routine textbook constant: it resolves a nonperiodic zero-temperature optimizer, explicit induced pressure law and three distinct rates, all using bounded-type orbit geometry. These precise asymptotic exponents could be used to compare thermodynamic sensitivity for low-complexity symbolic systems.
residual_risks: The proofs do not extend the rate exponents to all irrational slopes and do not compute rescaled limiting constants.

final_claim: For an arbitrary irrational Sturmian beta-shift the digit potential has a unique Sturmian maximizing measure and the exact positive-root weighted renewal pressure equation. For bounded-type slopes the pressure gap and entropy are Θ(t^{-1}), and the digit-density deficit is Θ(t^{-2}).
limitations: Best-of-knowledge O is constrained by uninspected full Huang arXiv:2610.03619 due institutional VPN/access; overlapping graph lemmas properly credited.
Rates hold only for fixed bounded-type slopes; no claim of a universal α-independent constant or exact tD(t) limit.
